title: Construct Target Array With Multiple Sums
statement: Let `n` be the length of `target`, and start from an array `arr` holding `n` ones. A move computes the current sum of all entries of `arr` and stores that sum at one position of your choice, overwriting the value there. You may make as many moves as you like, including none. Return `true` if some sequence of moves turns `arr` into exactly `target` (same value at every index), and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Going forward, every move has many choices; going backward there is only one. The sum only grows, so the last move wrote the largest entry, and that entry equals the sum before the move. With `largest` the biggest value and `rest` the sum of the others, the entry was `largest - rest` before. Undo moves until all values are `1` (yes) or a value cannot be explained (no). Undoing one move at a time is far too slow for `[1, 10^9]`, so `largest % rest` undoes all consecutive moves on that entry at once: it stays the biggest while it is above `rest`.

## Approach

1. Push every value into a max-heap and keep their sum in `total`.
2. Pop `largest` and compute `rest = total - largest`.
3. If `largest` is `1`, every value is `1`: return `true`. If `rest` is `1` (two values, the other is `1`), any `largest` can be built: return `true`.
4. If `rest` is `0` (a single value above `1`) or `largest <= rest`, no move could have produced it: return `false`.
5. Set `previous = largest % rest`. If it is `0`, undoing would stop at exactly `rest`, the sum of the others; then no entry exceeds the sum of the rest, so no move could have built that state: return `false`.
6. Push `previous`, set `total = rest + previous`, and repeat.

## Example 1, step by step

`target = [9, 3, 5]`, `total = 17`. Pop `9`: `rest = 8`, `previous = 1`, `total = 9`. Pop `5`: `rest = 4`, `previous = 1`, `total = 5`. Pop `3`: `rest = 2`, `previous = 1`, `total = 3`. Pop `1`: everything is `1`, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n + log(max) · log n): building the heap, then O(log max) rounds (each cuts `total` to at most two thirds) of O(log n) heap work.
- Space: O(n) for the heap.

## Pitfalls

- Subtracting `rest` once per loop times out on inputs like `[1, 10^9]`; use the remainder.
- `rest === 1` must return `true` before the remainder, because `x % 1` is always `0`.
- The sum of `5 * 10^4` values up to `10^9` exceeds 32-bit integers; use 64-bit totals in Java or C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | max-heap of the current values |
| `total` | sum of the current values |
| `largest` | the biggest value, the one the last move wrote |
| `rest` | sum of all other values |
| `previous` | the value at that position after undoing the moves |
